benchmark_kind: viability of a real DORAM (recursive Path ORAM) under the declared 2-of-3 semi-honest dishonest-majority threat model
scope_warning: Compile-time operation counts from MP-SPDZ, not executed runs, at N=1024/4096/16384 with a 64-bit entry size. MetaQA-scale figures are EXTRAPOLATIONS using O(n log^2 n) for the initialisation sort and O(log^2 n) for access. Nothing here is a malicious-security result.
question: The README records that a previous OptimalORAM attempt was abandoned because initialisation needed 'billions of preprocessing operations'. Compiler/oram.py provides batch_init, which bulk-loads an ORAM with one oblivious shuffle and sort instead of N oblivious writes. Does batch_init make a DORAM-backed hybrid viable?
method: Compile the same probe at fixed N with 1 access and with 9 accesses; the difference over 8 isolates per-access cost, and the remainder is one-time initialisation.

linear_oram_n1024.note: OptimalORAM selects LinearORAM below its threshold; this is a scan, and it is the baseline to beat

recursive_oram_n16384.note: the 13000x jump from N=4096 to N=16384 is OptimalORAM crossing from LinearORAM to RecursiveORAM, not a scaling effect

findings.doram_penalty_at_n16384: 5.1x WORSE per access than a linear scan
findings.batch_init_is_the_wall: batch_init at N=16384 costs 1.39 billion triples, which is 4200x the cost of one access. It is dominated by an oblivious sort of ~2N entries, so it does not go away with tuning.

conclusion: Under this threat model a DORAM only starts winning per access above roughly 83k entries, and its one-time initialisation needs about 1,200 queries in a SINGLE MP-SPDZ program run to amortise at MetaQA scale. The batch cap is 10, and there is no persistent ORAM state across runs, so the initialisation is paid every run. A DORAM-backed hybrid is therefore not the right design here, and this is a quantitative confirmation of the qualitative note already in the README rather than a new obstacle.
what_this_does_not_show: That DORAM is unviable under other threat models; honest-majority protocols make every secure operation far cheaper and would move all of these numbers.
That a persistent, cross-run ORAM would not amortise; that is a different system design and is not implemented.
Executed wall-clock or communication figures; these are compile-time operation counts.
That a hand-built ORAM variant could not beat MP-SPDZ's RecursiveORAM constants.
